reference: McShane LM et al. J Natl Cancer Inst 2005;97:1180-4; Altman DG et al. PLoS Med 2012;9:e1001216
methods: Candidate markers (n = 30) were screened for association with time / event in 180 patients (101 events) with SurvStudio 0.4.0.dev0. Each marker was tested for added value over the clinical covariates (z) with a Cox score test against the model with the clinical covariates alone, using the Efron method for tied event times. Multiplicity was assessed with Westfall-Young step-down max-T p-values from 999 permutations; for added value, the residuals of each marker after regression on the clinical covariates were permuted (Smith method; Winkler et al. 2014), approximating a conditional null under exchangeable residuals after linear adjustment, and the false discovery rate was estimated from the same permutations. Permutation inference requires exchangeability under the chosen null; strong family-wise error control also requires subset pivotality. Nonlinear marker-covariate relations can invalidate the residual-permutation calibration. Added-value testing also requires a suitable clinical Cox baseline: its functional form and proportional-hazards assumptions need checking. Multiplicity adjustment does not establish model adequacy. The screening procedure was not repeated on subsamples, so the stability of the selection was not assessed. Without subsamples the stability rule could not be applied, so no marker could be called robust; markers with a family-wise p-value at most 0.05 or a permutation q-value at most 0.1 were called suggestive, and markers without sufficient evidence of added value but with a marginal family-wise p-value at most 0.05 were called marginal only. Markers with more than 20% missing values, a constant value or more than 90% of patients at one value were excluded before testing (a filter blind to the outcome); other missing marker values were replaced by the marker's median among the patients in each fit, and patients with a missing or invalid outcome or stratum were excluded; missing clinical values used training-only imputation. Markers were analysed as continuous variables without cut-points. Patients with identical values on every marker were flagged as possible repeated samples; near-identical profiles are checked only on panels of at least 200 markers. No marker was selected, so the final Cox model held the clinical covariates only; its apparent C-index could not be adjusted for the subsampling gap because no subsample was available. Clinical basis: linear; training-only imputation, encoding and fixed knots were refitted in each training subset. Clinical PH/functional-form diagnostics and all-marker residual HC3 mean/variance diagnostics formed separate Holm families, with withholding at 1%. Method version marker-inference/2; inference status withheld. Inference depends on model and permutation assumptions; diagnostics do not certify them.
results: Added-value inference and robust marker claims were withheld. Standard inferential p/q values are unavailable, rather than zero; raw computations are retained separately for exploration. Any fitted prediction model and its performance estimates are exploratory. Inference depends on model and permutation assumptions; diagnostics do not certify them. Finite main-study engineering gates in prespecified supported conditions; not universal 5% error control or certification of an individual dataset. The 500-subject, 300-marker and 3000-marker extensions do not establish broader qualification. In particular, large independent and linear marker families substantially reduce availability; power retention and conditional error bounds also remain limiting. The screen for repeated samples flagged no patients.

items.topic: Handling of marker values and cut-points
items.text: Markers were analysed as continuous variables; the evaluation used no cut-points. Any cut-point used for figures should be fixed before looking at the outcome.

items.topic: Patient flow, numbers analysed and events
items.text: 180 patients with 101 events were analysed; no rows were excluded.

items.topic: Relation of the markers to standard prognostic variables
items.text: Added-value inference was withheld; no absence-of-added-value claim is supported. Show how the reported markers relate to the standard prognostic variables.

The marker table gives every marker's unadjusted score-test p-value (Unadjusted P) and, for all 30 markers, the hazard ratio from an unadjusted Cox model as a point estimate (Unadjusted HR); the table's confidence intervals belong to the adjusted hazard ratios. Kaplan-Meier curves by marker level can be drawn in the Survival curves tab with a cut-point fixed in advance.

The marker table gives, for all 30 markers, hazard ratios with 95% Wald confidence intervals from Cox models with the clinical covariates. Report the final model with all its variables from the Cox model tab.

items.topic: Marker effects adjusted for standard prognostic variables regardless of significance
items.text: Adjusted hazard ratios with confidence intervals are given for all 30 markers, whether or not they are significant.

items.topic: Further investigations: assumptions, sensitivity, internal validation
items.text: No internal validation was done: no subsamples were drawn, so neither the stability of the selection nor the optimism of the model's C-index was assessed. Check proportional hazards for the reported markers in the Cox model tab.
